Triage update (quick):
- Observed in traces: repeated identical requests from BrightLayer client within seconds after initial 504/timeout. Pattern consistent with zero-delay retries and high retry count.
- Representative snippet from trace IDs (attached in retry-traces.zip):
  - 2027-05-02T08:44:12Z client->api/redwood v=1 requestId=rl-7f2 status=timeout
  - 2027-05-02T08:44:12Z client->api/redwood v=1 requestId=rl-7f2 retry#1 backoff=0ms
  - 2027-05-02T08:44:12Z client->api/redwood v=1 requestId=rl-7f2 retry#2 backoff=0ms
  - repeated ~8 more times -> host saturation -> 5xx surge
- Root cause (initial read): BrightLayer's load test config left SDK defaults overridden (retries=10, backoff_ms=0). This configuration will amplify transient errors into a retry storm.

Action taken so far:
- Created INF ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-4821
- Prepared a short mitigation playbook.
- We can enforce a temporary connection-level rate limit for BrightLayer from the edge for the next 60–120 minutes to keep overall queueing bounded while they roll back config.

Recommendations for BrightLayer (short-term):
1) Set SDK retries=1 and enable exponential backoff with an initial delay of 100ms and multiplier 2.
2) Cap outstanding in-flight requests per client host (suggest 8).
3) If you must load-test, use a dedicated sandbox deployment not the production endpoint.
